# Changelog

All notable changes to `@absolutejs/absolute`.

This file is generated by `absolute-changelog` from the entries in
`changelog/`. Edit an entry, not this file — and add new ones under
`changelog/unreleased/`.

## 0.20.0-beta.175 — 2026-11-14

### Fixed

- **Angular hot updates no longer break the Content Security Policy under secureHeaders()**
  With `secureHeaders()` on, every Angular hot update in dev (a template, style or component edit) logged "Applying inline style violates the following Content Security Policy directive 'style-src …'", and the browser dropped the updated styles. Angular's browser bootstrap never received the page's CSP nonce, so the `<style>` elements it added after the server render had none. Angular pages and Angular islands now pass the nonce to Angular (`CSP_NONCE`) in the browser, in dev and in production, so hot-updated styles and styles for components rendered only in the browser are allowed.
- **`absolute dev` no longer restarts the server for a directory change event**
  The first `absolute dev` boot of a freshly copied project could log `Server file changed: src/backend/assets — restarting...` and restart the server once, because the file watcher reported the `assets` directory itself and a path with no file extension was treated like `.env`. Directory events no longer restart the dev server; changes to the files inside a directory are still handled through their own events.
- **`absolute dev` logs one `hmr update` per save of a server file**
  Saving a server file such as `src/backend/api.ts` under `absolute dev` printed `[hmr] hmr update src/backend/api.ts` two or more times, because an editor save reaches the watcher as several events and each one got past the "content unchanged" check before the first had recorded the new content. The edit was applied once; now it is also logged once.
- **Island pages get HMR in dev: island edits swap in place without a reload**
  In `absolute dev`, pages that render islands now update like any other page. Editing an island component (a React, Svelte or Vue file listed in your island registry, or a file it imports) rebuilds that island and swaps it into the open page without a reload: the edited island starts over from its props, the page and its other islands keep their state, and island stores keep their values. The next reload renders the edit on the server too, so the hydration-mismatch overlay no longer appears. Before, a React island edit left the browser on the old island bundle (every reload then failed hydration), and a Svelte or Vue island edit changed nothing at all. Editing the React page that hosts the islands, or a component it imports, also updates in place again; before, the update could leave lifeless copies of the islands on screen. This covers islands rendered by React and HTML pages, and the island registry may live outside your framework directories (for example `src/islands/`). Angular islands, and edits to the registry file itself, still reload the page.
- **Errors thrown by routes are logged for API and fetch requests too, not only page requests**
  When your app has no `onError` of its own, a route that throws was only logged for page and HTMX requests, and only when the project had an HTML or HTMX `error.html`. The same route called with `fetch` or `curl` (`Accept: */*`) or asking for JSON returned Elysia's generic 500 and wrote nothing to the log, in development and production, so a mistyped `asset()` key in an API route failed silently. Every unhandled route error is now logged once on the server, with the method, path and stack, whatever the request accepts. Responses are unchanged: the error details stay out of the response body, 404s and thrown `status(...)` responses are not logged, and an app that registers its own `onError` still handles (and logs) errors itself.
- **React Server Components pages named `*RSC.tsx` no longer get a doubled `RSCRSC` manifest key** (`asset`, `BaseBuildConfig`)
  A React Server Components page whose file name already ends in RSC got the suffix twice: `pages/HomeRSC.tsx` was `asset(manifest, 'HomeRSCRSC')`, so the natural `'HomeRSC'` was missing from the manifest and the route failed only at request time. Such a page is now `asset(manifest, 'HomeRSC')`. The doubled key still works as a deprecated alias for the same bundle and prints a one-time warning in dev naming the new key. If `pages/Home.tsx` and `pages/HomeRSC.tsx` both exist, `Home.tsx` keeps `HomeRSC` (its key is unchanged), `HomeRSC.tsx` stays at `HomeRSCRSC`, and the build warns about the clash.
- **`@absolutejs/absolute/react/components` can be imported from React Server Components** (`SuspenseSlot`, `StreamSlot`, `Link`)
  Importing anything from `@absolutejs/absolute/react/components` (for example `SuspenseSlot`) in a React Server Component crashed the page with `TypeError: createContext is not a function`, because the entry also defines `Link`'s context and React's server build has no `createContext`. A server component that imports the entry now gets a server components version of it: `SuspenseSlot`, `StreamSlot`, `Head`, `Image` and `JsonLd` render on the server as before, and `Link` and `usePrefetch` come from a "use client" module, so a server component can render `<Link>` and it hydrates as a client component. Wrapping these in your own 'use client' file is no longer needed. As with any client component, `<Link>` props passed from a server component must be serializable (no event handlers).
- **HTML and HTMX error and not-found pages load their stylesheets in production**
  The HTML and HTMX `error.html`, `not-found.html` and `loading.html` pages were copied into the build as written, so a stylesheet or script linked relative to the source (such as `../../styles/indexes/site.css`) returned 404 and the error page showed unstyled. These pages now get the same hashed asset URLs (and font tags) as your other HTML and HTMX pages.
- **Svelte component style edits now apply in dev without a reload**
  Editing only the `<style>` block of a Svelte component in dev hot-updated the component, but the page kept the old styles until a full reload: the browser reused the component's previously loaded stylesheet module. Each version of a component's styles now gets its own URL, so style edits apply immediately.

## 0.20.0-beta.174 — 2026-11-14

### Changed

- **Servers start faster: the framework no longer loads TypeScript at import**
  Importing `@absolutejs/absolute` (and its `build`, `angular`, `angular/server` and `mobile` entry points) loaded the `typescript` package straight away, which takes a few hundred milliseconds of CPU, even though a running server never needs it. TypeScript now loads the first time the framework actually uses it (route scanning, island registries, Angular compilation, config editing), so servers start faster. Nothing you call changed, and those functions stay synchronous.

## 0.20.0-beta.173 — 2026-11-14

### Security

- **Island pages no longer expose server file paths in production**
  In production, a React page that rendered an <Island> could put absolute paths from the server’s disk (server-rendered pages, server bundles and static HTML pages) into the manifest it embeds for the browser, exposing the server’s file layout. The manifest embedded in island pages now contains only browser URLs, whichever framework renders the page. No code changes are needed; rebuild and redeploy to pick up the fix.
- **Vue lazy route components no longer reveal the build machine’s file paths**
  A Vue page that exports `routes` and lazily loads a route component shipped the build machine’s absolute project path to every browser: the lazy component’s file name, and the imports of it in the router page and a shared chunk, read like `vue/client/sources/%2F/home/you/app/src/frontend/vue/components/Lazy.<hash>.js`. Compiled Vue files are now named by their path inside the project, such as `vue/client/sources/src/frontend/vue/components/Lazy.<hash>.js`, in both the browser and the server build. A Vue file outside the project, such as a package in a parent `node_modules` or a sibling workspace, is placed under `_external/` and named only by its path below the folder it shares with the project, or by a hash when that folder is the filesystem root. Rebuild and redeploy to stop serving the old paths.

### Changed

- **React pages stream SuspenseSlot and StreamSlot content without opting in** (`handleReactPageRequest`)
  A React page that rendered a `<SuspenseSlot>` or `<StreamSlot>` only streamed when its handler passed `collectStreamingSlots: true`. Without it the slot stayed on its fallback forever, and production logged nothing. `handleReactPageRequest` and the React Server Components page handler now collect streaming slots by default, so the shell arrives first and each slot's content streams in when it resolves. A page that renders no slot gets the same bytes and headers as before, with no measurable extra work. Pass `collectStreamingSlots: false` to turn collection off for a route; a slot rendered there logs a warning naming that option, once per render in development and once per process in production. Svelte, Vue and Angular handlers still need `collectStreamingSlots: true`, and their warning about the missing option now shows in production too.

### Fixed

- **Angular `@defer` sections stay on the page after hydration**
  An Angular page with `@defer` blocks streamed its deferred sections correctly, then lost them once the browser hydrated the page, in dev and in production. The browser logged `ReferenceError: process is not defined` from the defer slot, and dev also logged an NG0100 error. The defer slot no longer runs its server-only streaming setup in the browser, and the NODE_ENV check that streaming slots share no longer throws where there is no `process`, which also protects Svelte and Vue streaming slots that reach the browser. Deferred sections now stay resolved after hydration, with no console errors.
- **Editing a module server.ts imports updates the dev server again**
  In dev, editing a server module that server.ts imports, such as the api.ts a create-absolutejs app passes to .use(), updates the running server in place again: the new route responses are served without a restart, and scopedState keeps every visitor’s state. Before, when the project’s folder path contained "angular" (or "ember"), the edit was mistaken for an Angular component and sent to Angular HMR, or silently dropped when Angular was not configured, and the old response kept being served until dev restarted, even after later server.ts edits. A .ts file outside every configured framework directory is now always treated as server or shared code, and a server.ts edit also applies any imported module whose file changed but whose update never arrived.
- **Dev serves source files whose paths contain spaces**
  The dev module server now decodes the percent-encoding a browser adds to module URLs. Before, a source file whose path contained a space or another encoded character, such as a project or linked package inside a folder named "Local Documents", was requested as `%20` and answered with a 500, so the page failed to hydrate in `absolute dev`.
- **absolute doctor reports a busy dev port as in use**
  absolute doctor could say the dev port was free while another server was listening on it, most visibly on macOS, where its process lookup failed silently and found no listeners. It now checks the port directly: it tries to connect over IPv4 and IPv6 loopback and to bind the IPv4 and IPv6 wildcard addresses separately, so a listener on either family or on both is reported as in use. The port it checks is resolved the same way as absolute dev (ABSOLUTE_PORT, then PORT, then dev.port in absolute.config.ts, then the default), and the check also runs when the config file cannot be loaded.
- **Builds that import react/router without react-router installed explain why, and point to a Link that needs no router**
  Importing `<Link>` from `@absolutejs/absolute/react/router` in a project without the optional `react-router` package failed the build with a bare `Could not resolve: "react-router"`. That entry also exports `<UniversalRouter>`, which is built on react-router, so it does need the package. The build now says so, tells you to install react-router for `<UniversalRouter>`, and points to `import { Link } from '@absolutejs/absolute/react/components'`: the same `<Link>`, with no react-router dependency, whose clicks `enableNavigation()` turns into soft page navigations. A react-router import in your own code without the package installed gets the same advice.

### Internal

- **DeferSlotComponent’s declaration gains a private member** (`DeferSlotComponent`)
  The published type declaration of `DeferSlotComponent` lists a new private member, used to tell the server render from the browser. Nothing about how the component is used in templates changed.

## 0.20.0-beta.172 — 2026-11-13

### Changed

- **absolute typecheck checks Vue projects with vue-check**
  For a project with Vue, `absolute typecheck` now runs vue-check (`@absolutejs/vue-check`, a dependency of the framework) instead of vue-tsc whenever it runs bun check: the project’s own Vue codegen with Bun’s native checker, reporting the errors vue-tsc reports in a fraction of the time and memory. Its generated TypeScript stays in `.absolutejs/vue-check`. vue-tsc remains the fallback where tsc does: Bun older than 1.4.4, or `ABSOLUTE_TYPECHECK_CHECKER=tsc`.

### Fixed

- **absolute typecheck type-checks even when the project has a check script**
  When a project’s package.json has a `check` script, `bun check` runs that script instead of type-checking, so `absolute typecheck` could report a project as checked without checking it. It now always passes `--no-script`, which Bun added in 1.4.4, and so uses bun check from Bun 1.4.4 on (it was 1.4.3). On Bun 1.4.3 it type-checks with tsc, as on older Bun.

## 0.20.0-beta.171 — 2026-11-13

### Security

- **Production error pages show a generic message instead of the error text**
  Error convention pages showed the error's own message outside development. A missing static page rendered `error.html` with `{{ message }}` set to "ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/srv/app/build/html/pages/Nope.html'", which exposed the server's file layout. Database and network errors can expose hosts and queries the same way. Outside development, every error convention page (HTML and HTMX `error.html`, and the React, Svelte, Vue and Angular error pages) now receives the message "Something went wrong while rendering this page." and no stack. The built-in error page shown when no convention exists does the same. The `name` prop is unchanged. The full error is still logged on the server, and development still shows the real message and stack.
- **Production no longer serves /manifest.json or puts server file paths in island pages**
  Under `absolute start`, `GET /manifest.json` returned the build's runtime manifest, which lists the absolute disk path of every SSR page and server bundle (for example `/srv/app/build/react/server/rsc/Dashboard.<hash>.js`). It now returns 404, as `server-outputs.json` and `spa-routes.json` already did, and so do its `.br` and `.gz` copies. The browser never fetched this file. Pages with islands also carried those paths in the inline `window.__ABSOLUTE_MANIFEST__` script. That script now holds only web paths, so island bundles and the islands bootstrap resolve as before. A web-app manifest can no longer be named `manifest.json`: the build overwrote that file with its own manifest, so it was never served. `pwa.manifest.path: '/manifest.json'` is now a build error, and a `manifest.json` in `publicDirectory` logs a warning. Use the default `/manifest.webmanifest`.

### Changed

- **The bundled htmx is now 2.0.11**
  The htmx copy that `absolute add htmx` installs, and that `absolute htmx` reports as the vendored version, is now 2.0.11 instead of 2.0.6. Projects that already have htmx keep their installed copy. Run `absolute htmx 2.0.11` to upgrade one.
- **Routes that throw render error.html for HTML and HTMX page requests**
  A route handler that threw before returning an HTML or HTMX page got Elysia's JSON 500. Browser navigations and HTMX requests now get the `error.html` from the HTML or HTMX pages directory, with status 500. HTMX requests try the HTMX one first. In production the page shows a generic message and no stack. Other requests, Elysia's own errors and thrown `status(...)` responses are unchanged. This is a fallback: if your app registers its own `onError`, before or after `.use(absolutejs)`, your handler keeps handling these errors and no `error.html` is rendered. The app's handlers are found when the server starts with `.listen()`; an app that only calls `app.handle()` gets `error.html` regardless. See docs/STATIC_PAGE_CONVENTIONS.md.

### Fixed

- **Angular APP_BASE_HREF works when the page handler is called from a helper**
  An Angular router page mounted at a wildcard route like `.get('/portal/*', …)` only got `APP_BASE_HREF` when `handleAngularPageRequest(...)` was written directly inside that route. Called from a helper function, no base href was set and the router could not match any route. The base href now comes from the route that matched the request, so `/portal/*` gives `/portal/` wherever the handler call is written, and the browser bootstraps with the same value. Parameterised mounts such as `/t/:tenant/*` use the values from the request URL. A provider you pass in the handler's `providers` option still takes precedence on the server.
- **Angular router pages with routed children in the same file render the right root**
  When an Angular page module exported `routes` and declared its routed child components in the same file, the build picked the first exported class as the page, so the server and the browser rendered the first routed child as the page root for every URL. The page is now the component that hosts `<router-outlet>`. Without an outlet, the last exported component is the page, and an explicit `export default` still wins.
- **No more false "2 distinct @angular/core resolutions" warning, and doctor finds real duplicates**
  Production builds of Angular pages that import `@absolutejs/absolute/angular` warned "Server bundle references 2 distinct @angular/core resolutions" even though every real import used the same copy. The check read text such as `from '@angular/core'` inside string literals in AbsoluteJS's own code as imports. It now reads the bundle's actual imports. `absolute doctor` also checks that each `@angular/*` runtime package resolves to one physical copy, and `absolute doctor --fix` pins your app's version in `overrides`, removes the extra copy and reinstalls.
- **Angular dev rebuilds no longer fail on React or Svelte when they are not installed**
  In a project without React or Svelte installed, such as a Vue and Angular app, every Angular rebuild in `absolute dev` logged "angular client bundle rebuild failed" with "Could not resolve: react" and "svelte", and the served bundle stayed on its previous version. The Angular dev rebuild now stubs frameworks the project does not install, like the initial build already did.
- **Backend HMR keeps scoped state created inline in the app, the way create-absolutejs writes it**
  A project made with create-absolutejs creates its scoped state inline: `.use([absolutejs, api, scopedState({ count: { value: 0 } })])`. Editing `server.ts` or `api.ts` re-runs that statement, and `@absolutejs/scoped-state` 0.3 keeps every visitor's session inside the plugin `scopedState()` returns, so each edit made a new, empty one and every count went back to 0. Backend HMR now hands the re-run statement the plugin the same call made last time, so visitors keep their state. This works for any number of `scopedState()` calls in a statement. A call whose arguments you edit starts empty, and the dev server says so. A call you delete is dropped. When the arguments are not plain literals, for example a variable, the call cannot be matched safely, so it still starts empty and the dev server warns you to move it into its own top-level `const` and pass that to `.use()`.
- **Dev watchers ignore editor temp, swap and lock files**
  The dev server treated some editor and tool temp files as source changes. On macOS, `sed -i` writes a `.!12345!file.ts` file, which made an Angular page rebootstrap and lose its state. The dev watchers, including the one that restarts the server, now ignore `sed -i` temp files from both GNU and macOS, Vim swap files and its `4913` probe, Emacs lock and autosave files, `~` backups, `.tmp` files, JetBrains `___jb_tmp___` and `___jb_old___` files, Chrome `.crswap` files, Kate swap files and gedit's `.goutputstream-` files. The saved file's own change still triggers the update.
- **Editing a shared partial in dev updates each open HTML or HTMX page with its own content and the new text**
  With two HTML or HTMX pages open that share a partial or layout, editing the partial made every tab show the last page updated. Both tabs showed the same body, and one lost its own `<title>` and other slot content. Each tab now applies only its own page. Live updates also stopped putting the old text back on elements that have an `id`, so an edited partial or page shows its new text there too. Text that a script changed on such an element is still kept.
- **Production warnings start with [absolutejs] instead of [hmr]**
  Warnings and errors from a production server or build, such as "File route ... is not served", started with `[hmr]` even though production has no HMR. They now start with `[absolutejs]`. The dev server still uses `[hmr]`.
- **React islands render in production builds** (`Island`)
  A React page that rendered a React `<Island>` returned 500 under `absolute start` with `renderToString is not a function`. Island SSR used React's legacy string renderer, which the production server bundle strips out. Islands now render with `renderToReadableStream`. When the island registry has React islands, the production server bundle also keeps React external. Each island's source loads `react` from node_modules when it first renders, and a second copy inlined into the bundle made the island's hooks fail.
- **Production builds no longer leave old hashed bundles in the build directory**
  A production build now removes the bundles an earlier build left in the build directory. The cleanup only recognised file hashes made of hex digits, but Bun hashes use letters and digits, so old server bundles, page bundles, workers, fonts and React Server Components bundles piled up with every build. A build now removes older versions of the files it writes, old chunks in the directories it writes chunks to, the `.br` and `.gz` copies of removed files, and the outputs of pages that no longer exist. It keeps a list of its outputs in `build-outputs.json` to find those, and that file is never served. Files you put in the build directory yourself are left alone.
- **Svelte router pages, and pages whose only content is one component, hydrate without a mismatch warning in dev**
  In dev, every page using the Svelte router logged `[svelte] hydration_mismatch` and was mounted again from scratch, even a page with one `<Route>`. The same happened to any Svelte page or snippet whose only content is one component. The dev server compiles browser components with Svelte's HMR option, which expects a marker comment after such a component, but the server render was compiled without it and left the markers out. The server render now uses the same option in dev, so these pages hydrate cleanly. Production builds were not affected.
- **`absolute typecheck` accepts imports of Svelte components that have no `<script>` block**
  Importing a `.svelte` component that has no `<script>` block failed `absolute typecheck` with "Could not find a declaration file for module", unless the project's tsconfig set `allowJs`. svelte-check treats a component without `<script lang="ts">` as JavaScript, and without `allowJs` it could not resolve the import. The svelte-check step now enables `allowJs` in the config it generates. JavaScript files are still not type-checked unless the project sets `checkJs`. The generated declaration for such a component, used when server code imports it, is now a complete TypeScript declaration instead of one that names `SvelteComponent` without importing it.
- **Vue pages that export `routes` work in production builds** (`defineRoutes`, `handleVuePageRequest`)
  A Vue page that exported `routes` returned 500 under `absolute start` with `__VUE_PROD_DEVTOOLS__ is not defined`. vue-router is bundled into the page's server build and reads Vue's compile-time feature flags, which only the client builds defined. The flags are now defined in the server build, the production server bundle, `absolute compile`, the dev dependency vendor and the dev module server. Lazily loaded route components also failed to load in production with a 404, because their build path contains a directory named `%2F` and the server decoded it into a slash. They now load, so a direct visit to a nested URL mounts the route and client-side navigation works.

### Internal

- **Mobile release functions’ declarations reorder their result members** (`buildAbsoluteAndroidRelease`, `buildAbsoluteIosRelease`, `buildAbsoluteRemoteIosRelease`, `createAbsoluteMobileCompatibilityArtifact`, `installAbsoluteIosRelease`, `parseAbsoluteMobileCompatibilityArtifact`, `readAbsoluteMobileMaterializedReleases`)
  The published type declarations of these mobile release functions list the members of their inferred result types in a different order. The types are the same; nothing about how they are called or what they return changed.

## 0.20.0-beta.170 — 2026-11-13

### Breaking

- **Two pages with the same name in the HTML and HTMX directories are a build error instead of one silently replacing the other** (`asset`, `build`)
  An HTML page and an HTMX page with the same file name (both `pages/Home.html`) share the manifest key `Home`. The build only warned "Manifest key collision … overwritten", and both routes then served whichever page was processed last. The build now fails and names both source files. In dev the error is reported like any other failed build pass. Key naming is unchanged.
  _Migration:_ If the build reports "Manifest key \"…\" belongs to two pages", rename one of the two files (for example `htmx/pages/Home.html` to `htmx/pages/HtmxHome.html`) and update the `asset(manifest, …)` call in its route. Builds without a collision are unaffected.
- **Svelte `{#await}` blocks render and hydrate natively; server streaming is opt-in with `<!-- absolute:stream -->`** (`handleSveltePageRequest`)
  Every `{#await}` with a pending branch was rewritten into a streaming slot, and any page containing one had hydration switched off. Buttons on such a page never worked; without `collectStreamingSlots: true` the pending branch showed forever; with it, a component in the `then` branch arrived as literal text; `{#if}` inside a branch failed to compile; and a shorthand `{#await x then y}` followed by a normal block failed with "Unterminated regular expression", because the pattern matched across both. A plain `{#await}` is now left to Svelte, which renders the pending branch on the server and resolves and hydrates it in the browser. Streaming is opt-in with `<!-- absolute:stream -->` directly before the block. A streamed block's branches are sent as HTML, so a component or logic block inside one is a build error, and only pages that stream a block skip hydration.
  _Migration:_ To keep server-side streaming for an `{#await}` block, put `<!-- absolute:stream -->` directly before it and keep its branches to elements and `{expressions}`. Unmarked blocks now render the pending branch on the server and resolve in the browser.

### Removed

- **Remove the unimplemented `pageRouterPlugin` export** (`pageRouterPlugin`)
  `pageRouterPlugin` was a placeholder that only logged "Page Router Plugin Not Implemented Yet" and registered nothing, so removing it changes no behavior.
  _Migration:_ Delete the `pageRouterPlugin` import and call; it never did anything. Register page routes with Elysia (`.get(path, () => handle…PageRequest(…))`) as before.

### Security

- **Initial props, request context, island state and JSON-LD can no longer break out of their inline <script>**
  Vue and Ember wrote a page's initial props into an inline script with a plain `JSON.stringify`, so a prop value containing `</script>` ended the script and the rest of the value was parsed as HTML: an XSS hole for any page that passes user-provided data as props. The same applied to Angular's `requestContext`, the island state and manifest scripts, and JSON-LD (`generateHeadElement`, the React and Svelte `JsonLd` components). All of these now escape `<`, U+2028 and U+2029, as React and Svelte page props already did. The data is unchanged once parsed.
- **Production servers no longer run development code paths: error pages stop exposing stacks, and `client: 'none'` Vue pages stop shipping the dev reload client**
  Bun's bundler replaces a literal `process.env.NODE_ENV` with its build-time value, and with nothing defined that value is "development". The published dist/ was built that way, so every such check was a constant: `absolute start` and compiled binaries ran development code with NODE_ENV=production. Error convention pages received `error.stack`; Vue pages with `client: 'none'` shipped the ~130 KB inline dev reload client; React pages emitted the Fast Refresh setup; Angular pages stat'ed their module on every request; and the island-bootstrap and streaming-slot dev warnings stayed on. The library build now leaves `process.env.NODE_ENV` a runtime read, the source reads it through `src/utils/runtimeMode.ts`, and a lint rule rejects a literal `process.env.NODE_ENV` in src/.
- **Production servers no longer serve their own server bundle, SSR bundles or runtime manifests as static files**
  `absolute start` writes the bundled server into the build directory, and that directory is also the static root, so `GET /server.js` downloaded the whole backend. The same applied to its `.br`/`.gz` copies, to the Svelte/Vue/Angular SSR page bundles under `<framework>/server/`, to the compiled convention pages, and to `absolute-runtime.json`, `conventions.json` and `spa-routes.json`. Production static serving now excludes those, plus `.map` files and native `.node` addons. The build records every file its server pass writes in `server-outputs.json`, and those are excluded by exact path, so SSR bundles are covered wherever the layout of a project puts them (a Svelte-only build writes them to `svelte/pages/`, Angular to `angular/src/…`). The precompressed handler applies the same list. The server still reads all of them from disk.

### Added

- **Angular pages can opt into zone.js change detection**
  Angular pages ran zoneless only, so apps and libraries that rely on zone.js (NgZone, change detection after timers or manually added event listeners) didn't update. Set `angular: { changeDetection: 'zone' }` in absolute.config.ts and add zone.js to your app (`bun add zone.js`). Server rendering then waits for the timers and requests a page starts, the browser loads zone.js before Angular boots, and hydration and HMR keep working. Async functions in your Angular code are compiled to generators in this mode, because zone.js can't follow native `await`. Elysia routes keep working with zone.js loaded on the server. The default stays zoneless. Angular islands still render zoneless in zone mode.
- **Links between pages built with different frameworks can navigate without a full page reload**
  Call `enableNavigation()` from `@absolutejs/absolute/client/navigation` on your pages and a link from a page in one framework to a page in another (a React page to a Svelte page, say) no longer reloads the browser. The target page's HTML is fetched, its stylesheets load first, the current page is torn down, the head and body are swapped (in a View Transition where the browser supports one), and the target page hydrates. Island stores made with `createIslandStore` keep their values, back and forward work across the two pages with their scroll positions, and the new page's title is announced to screen readers. Links inside a framework's own router still navigate through that router. Under `secureHeaders()` the swapped-in page's scripts and styles run with the current page's nonce, but only those that carried their own response's nonce. Add `data-absolute-navigation="off"` to a link (or a parent) to get a normal page load; any failure also falls back to one. The Svelte router's `<Link>` now leaves a URL that no mounted `<Router>` matches to this navigation when it is enabled. This release is tested with React and Svelte pages. Vue and Angular pages have the same teardown hook but are not tested yet. HTML and HTMX pages have none, so leaving one is still a normal page load.
- **Opt-in file routes for React and Svelte pages, with typed `load` functions** (`fileRoutes`, `reactFileRoute`, `svelteFileRoute`, `FileRouteContext`)
  Opt-in file routes for React and Svelte pages. With `fileRoutes: true` in absolute.config.ts, each file under `<reactDirectory>/routes/` or `<svelteDirectory>/routes/` becomes a GET route: `index.tsx` serves `/`, `blog/index.tsx` serves `/blog`, and `blog/[slug].tsx` serves `/blog/:slug`. Files and folders starting with `_` are private, so components can live next to routes. A sibling `blog/[slug].server.ts` can export `load`, whose result becomes the page's props, and `beforeHandle`, which can answer the request first (for example with a redirect). The build writes a route module (`src/routes.gen.ts` by default, `fileRoutes.output` to change it); pass its `routeTree` to `fileRoutes(routeTree, manifest)` after `prepare()`. The route module checks types: `load` must take the route's params and return the page's props, so a renamed param or a missing prop is a type error. Explicit routes stay the default and win over a file route for the same path. In `absolute dev`, adding, renaming or removing a route file updates the routes without a restart. Catch-all, optional and group segments, Vue, Angular and HTML routes, and per-folder conventions are planned. See docs/FILE_ROUTER_PLAN.md.
- **Form actions: one handler for forms that work without JavaScript and update in place with it, on React, static HTML and HTMX pages**
  `defineAction(path, { body, handler })` defines a form action: a POST route that checks the form against an Elysia `t.Object` schema and works with or without JavaScript. Without JavaScript a plain `<form method="post">` posts, the browser is sent back to the page (or to `redirect`) and the page shows the result: React and other SSR pages read it with `getActionState(action)` and pass it as a prop, and static HTML and HTMX pages get the errors, the success message and what the user typed written into `<form data-absolute-action>` by the server. With JavaScript, React's `useFormAction` hook (from `@absolutejs/absolute/react/hooks`) and `enhanceForms()` for plain pages (from `@absolutejs/absolute/client`) submit without a reload and expose pending, the typed result and one error message per field. HTMX `hx-post` forms get the action's `htmx` fragment, or behave like a plain post. Cross-site posts are refused (403), bodies over `maxBodySize` (default 10 MiB) are refused before they are read (413), and JSON clients such as Eden get JSON.
- **Layouts and partials for HTML and HTMX pages with `<abs-include>` and `<abs-slot>`**
  HTML and HTMX pages can share markup with `<abs-include src="../partials/header.html"></abs-include>`, which is replaced at build time with the file's contents. Paths are relative to the including file, and included files can include others. A layout marks where content goes with `<abs-slot>` and `<abs-slot name="head">`; a page fills the slots through the include's children and `<template slot="head">`. Includes are expanded before asset paths, image optimization and island rendering, so included markup gets all three. A missing file or an include cycle fails the build and shows the chain. Only the `.html` files directly in `pages/` are pages. In dev, editing a partial or layout updates every page that includes it. See docs/HTML_INCLUDES.md.
- **Internationalization: locale routing, typed ICU message catalogs, React and Svelte translation APIs, hreflang links and a per-locale sitemap** (`defineI18n`, `i18nPlugin`, `getRequestLocale`, `I18nProvider`, `useI18n`, `setI18n`, `getI18n`, `createTranslator`, `defineMessages`, `formatMessage`, `Metadata`, `generateHeadElement`, `Head`, `SitemapConfig`, `BaseBuildConfig`)
  Apps can now be translated. `defineI18n()` takes your locales, the default locale's messages and a loader for each other locale, and `i18nPlugin()` works out each request's locale from the URL prefix (`/fr/about`), the domain, or the visitor's cookie and `Accept-Language` header. Handlers get `locale` and an `i18n` object: `i18n.t('key', params)` formats ICU messages (plurals, select, numbers, dates) with the platform's `Intl`, and `i18n.payload(['namespace'])` returns the messages a page needs to hydrate, which you pass as a page prop. React pages read them with `I18nProvider` and `useI18n()` from `@absolutejs/absolute/react/hooks`; Svelte pages with `setI18n()` and `getI18n()` from `@absolutejs/absolute/svelte`. Message keys and their parameters are type-checked against the default catalog, and a locale missing a key is a type error. `i18n.alternates()` builds hreflang links, which the `alternates` field of `Metadata` renders in `generateHeadElement` and the React and Svelte `Head` components. Setting `sitemap.i18n` lists every page once per locale with hreflang alternates. Svelte pages get the request's `lang` and `dir` on `<html>`. The browser-safe helpers (`createTranslator`, `formatMessage`, `localizePath`, `negotiateLocale`, `localeDirection`) are exported from `@absolutejs/absolute/i18n`. See docs/I18N_PLAN.md.
- **Partial prerendering: pre-rendered React and Svelte pages serve a cached shell instantly and stream their `dynamic` slots per request** (`StreamSlot`, `SuspenseSlot`, `StreamingSlot`)
  A pre-rendered page used to be either fully cached or fully rendered per request. Now a streaming slot marked `dynamic` (`<StreamSlot dynamic>` or `<SuspenseSlot dynamic>` in React, the `dynamic` prop or `<!-- absolute:stream dynamic -->` in Svelte) stays a hole in the pre-rendered page. On a route listed in `static.routes`, the build stores the page as a static shell: other slots are resolved into it, and dynamic slots keep their fallback. Each request gets the cached shell at once, before the route handler runs. Only the dynamic slots are then rendered, with the visitor's cookies and headers, and streamed into the page, carrying the request's CSP nonce under `secureHeaders()`. Revalidation (`static.revalidate`) re-captures the shell. Pages without a dynamic slot are pre-rendered as before. Vue and Angular support comes later.
- **Opt-in React Server Components for React pages served from Elysia routes**
  Set `reactServerComponentsDirectory` in absolute.config.ts and put pages in its `pages` folder. Pages are server components: they can be async and read data directly, and that code never ships to the browser. Components marked `"use client"` are server-rendered, then hydrated in the browser. Serve a page from any Elysia route with `handleReactServerPageRequest({ page: asset(manifest, '<Page>RSC'), props })`. `<Suspense>` boundaries stream, and the inline scripts carry the CSP nonce when `secureHeaders()` is on. Install `react-server-dom-webpack` at the same version as `react` (19.2.3 or later). Existing React pages are unchanged. Server Actions, client-side navigation and HMR for these pages are not available yet; edits reload after the dev server restarts.
- **`secureHeaders()`: a strict nonce-based Content-Security-Policy and security headers for every framework** (`secureHeaders`, `getCspNonce`)
  `secureHeaders()` is an opt-in Elysia plugin that sends a Content-Security-Policy with a per-request nonce (`'strict-dynamic'`, no `'unsafe-inline'` for scripts), plus `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy`, `frame-ancestors` and `Permissions-Policy`, each overridable. Every inline `<script>` and `<style>` AbsoluteJS writes carries the nonce: page bootstraps and initial props for every framework, island state, streaming-slot patches, inline page CSS, Svelte and Angular component styles, speculation rules, the error pages and the dev HMR client. The nonce is added where each script is written, so a script injected through `{@html}` / `v-html` / `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` stays blocked. Pre-rendered and ISR pages store the nonce they were rendered with and swap it for each request's, on scripts, styles and `<link rel="modulepreload">`. A page pre-rendered without the plugin is served without a policy and logged. In development the policy also allows the HMR WebSocket and `'unsafe-eval'` (Angular's dev compiler). `getCspNonce()` and the `cspNonce` context value give your own inline scripts the nonce. See docs/SECURITY_HEADERS.md.
- **Self-hosted, preloaded fonts with layout-stable fallbacks from the `fonts` config**
  A new `fonts` option in `absolute.config.ts` downloads Google Fonts (or copies local font files) at build time and serves them from your own origin with content-hashed names and a one-year immutable cache. The build writes one linked stylesheet with `font-display: swap`, a size-adjusted fallback face per family so text does not shift while the font loads, and a `--font-<family>` variable and `.font-<family>` class. Pass `fontAssets(manifest)` to the `fonts` option of `Head` (React, Svelte) or `generateHeadElement`; HTML and HTMX pages get the preload and stylesheet tags automatically. Downloads are cached between builds; a failed download stops the build unless `fallbackToRemote` is set. Hashed static files served by a plain GET now also get the immutable cache header; before, only precompressed copies did.
- **Svelte router: route guards with server redirects, lazy routes, and scroll restoration** (`goto`, `beforeNavigate`, `redirect`, `preloadRoute`, `GotoOptions`, `renderToReadableStream`, `observeViewport`)
  Route guards: a `guard` on `<Route>` or `<Router>`, and `beforeNavigate()` for browser-only checks, runs before `<Link>` clicks, `goto()` and back/forward, and can be async. It returns nothing to allow, `false` to cancel or a URL / `redirect()` to redirect. Cancelling back/forward puts the URL back. Route and Router guards also run during the server render, where a redirect is a 302. Lazy routes: `<Route loader={() => import("./Page.svelte")}>` puts the component in its own chunk, loaded when the route is first visited or when a `<Link>` to it is prefetched, with optional `pending` and `error` snippets. The server renders the real component and the browser loads its chunk before hydrating, so the page doesn't flash. Scroll restoration: while a router is mounted, new navigations start at the top or at the `#hash` target, and back/forward and reload return to where you were. `goto(url, { noScroll: true })` leaves the scroll alone. `goto()` now resolves to what happened (`"committed"`, `"cancelled"`, `"redirected"`, …), and `history.state` holds the router's bookkeeping next to your state, which `page.state` still returns unchanged. Smaller additions that support this: `renderToReadableStream` takes a Svelte `context`, a `settle` callback that can ask for another render pass, and a function for `bootstrapScriptContent`; `observeViewport` and `scheduleHoverPrefetch` take an `onVisible` / `onPrefetch` callback; and the `noScroll` doc on `GotoOptions` now covers `#hash` targets.
- **Vue pages can load data on the server with `useServerData` and hydrate without a second fetch**
  Vue pages could only get server data as props from the route handler. `useServerData(key, fetcher)`, exported from `@absolutejs/absolute/vue`, runs the fetcher while the page renders on the server and writes the result into the page, so hydration shows it without fetching again. A client-side route change, a page that exports `routes`, or `server: false` fetches in the browser instead. It returns `data`, `error`, `pending` and `refresh` refs, with `data` typed from the fetcher. A fetcher that throws on the server renders an error state rather than failing the page (in production the message sent to the browser is generic). Using one key twice in a request fails the page with a clear error outside production. Pages with `client: 'none'` render the data but write nothing into the page, and streaming pages are supported. Streaming-slot patches also no longer land inside the page's own inline scripts.
- **Opt-in Core Web Vitals reporting with `vitals` and `onVital()`** (`onVital`)
  Set `vitals` in absolute.config.ts (`{ endpoint?, sampleRate?, dev? }`) to report LCP, INP, CLS, FCP and TTFB from real visits. A production build bundles a small reporter (web-vitals plus a sender) that every framework's client bundle imports and that static HTML/HTMX pages load with a script tag. Each page load samples once, and a page that reports sends one batch, with its route and navigation type, when it's hidden or closed (`sendBeacon`, falling back to `fetch` keepalive). `prepare()` serves `POST /__absolute/vitals`, validated with a TypeBox schema. It stores nothing; register `onVital(handler)` to forward the metrics to your own store. With `vitals` unset nothing is built or injected, and dev reports only with `dev: true`. It works on pre-rendered pages and under `secureHeaders()`. See docs/WEB_VITALS.md.

### Fixed

- **Angular HMR applies edits to components whose `styleUrl` is Less or Stylus, and reports style compile errors accurately**
  The surgical Angular HMR path compiled `styleUrl` files synchronously, which Less and Stylus don't support. Editing a component whose `styleUrl` was a `.less` or `.styl` file showed "Style file not found" for a file that existed, and the update stalled behind the error overlay. The fast path now compiles Less and Stylus with their async compilers. A style that exists but fails to compile reports the compiler's error instead of "not found". The production build and the dev rebuild path already handled Less and Stylus.
- **`absolute add` edits scaffolded configs, and generated Angular pages no longer import shared files**
  `absolute add <framework>` failed with "Could not find defineConfig" on the config create-absolutejs writes (`import { defineConfig } …` followed by `export default defineConfig({…})`). The config walker passed `pending.push(child)` straight to TypeScript's `forEachChild`, which stops at the first truthy callback result, so only a file's first statement (the import) was ever searched. The auth config readers behind `absolute config` had the same bug and are fixed too. `absolute generate page --framework angular` now writes a self-contained page with its nav baked in, like the static pages, instead of importing `../../shared/navData` from outside the Angular directory.
- **Production stack traces point at your server file and page components instead of the bundled output**
  The production server bundle had no source map, so errors logged by `absolute start` pointed into dist/server.js. The Svelte, Vue and Angular SSR page bundles had none either; only dev chained their maps back to the source. The server bundle now gets a linked map, and the SSR page bundles get the same inline-and-chained maps as dev. A route handler error points at its line in your server file, and a page component error at its `.svelte`/`.vue` file. Svelte frames used to name a nonexistent file next to the build output (`build/svelte/pages/Page.svelte`), because Svelte records the source by basename; they now resolve to the original file, in dev too. Neither map is served publicly. The "Could not decode sourcemap" warning was fixed in the previous release.
- **Production servers start when their build directory is read-only, such as in a container running as a non-root user**
  The image optimizer created its cache directory (`<build>/.cache/images` unless `images.cacheDirectory` is set) when the server started, so a production server that could not write its build directory crashed on boot with `EACCES` or `EROFS`, even if the app never optimized an image. That is the usual container setup: the build copied in as root and the server running as a non-root user, or a read-only root filesystem. The directory is now created on the first image written to the cache. When it cannot be written, images are still optimized and served, just not cached. A prepared build now starts from a read-only directory with an empty HOME and writes nothing outside TMPDIR.
- **`absolute start` no longer warns "Could not decode sourcemap in dist/server.js" on the first error**
  The production server bundle has no source map, but the AbsoluteJS code inside it builds inline source map comments for Svelte and Vue output. Those were template literals starting with `\n`, which Bun's bundler emits as a real newline, leaving a line that starts `//# sourceMappingURL=data:…${…}` in the middle of dist/server.js. Bun read that line as the bundle's own source map whenever it built a stack trace, and warned that it couldn't decode it.
- **HTML and HTMX pages render their error.html when they fail, and HTMX requests get the HTMX not-found.html** (`ConventionsMap`)
  `handleHTMLPageRequest` and `handleHTMXPageRequest` now render the error convention when a page can't be served (its file is missing or unreadable, or it fails a static-page check). They return status 500 with `<Page>.error.html` or `error.html`, like the framework handlers, and `{{ stack }}` is empty in production. Before, the error went unhandled. HTMX pages use the HTMX pages directory's error page first. An HTMX request (`HX-Request: true`) to an unknown route gets that directory's `not-found.html` first. Having `error.html` or `not-found.html` in both the HTML and HTMX directories no longer counts as a page name collision. `loading.html` doesn't apply to static pages; see docs/STATIC_PAGE_CONVENTIONS.md.
- **React `SuspenseSlot` content streams in production builds** (`SuspenseSlot`)
  `SuspenseSlot` rendered its resolved content with React's `renderToStaticMarkup`, but `absolute start` strips React's legacy string renderer out of the production server bundle to save about 4,000 lines. In production every SuspenseSlot patch failed with `renderToStaticMarkup is not a function`, so the fallback stayed on the page. The slot now renders with `renderToReadableStream`, which the bundle keeps.
- **Apps using the Svelte `Head` component build again**
  The packaged Svelte `Head` component imports a small icon helper by relative path, and the package shipped the component without that file, so any app using `Head` from `@absolutejs/absolute/svelte/components/Head.js` failed to build with "Could not resolve ../../utils/iconVersion". The helper now ships next to the components.
- **Svelte HMR keeps component state instead of remounting the page with a number read from the first button**
  On every Svelte component update the HMR client read the first number out of the page's first `<button>`, stored it in sessionStorage and remounted the page with it as an `initialCount` prop. On a page whose first button said "Page 1", editing any component reset a counter elsewhere on the page and injected `initialCount: 1`. The scaffold's demo only worked because its first button happened to be the counter. The client now leaves state to Svelte's own HMR and never reads it from the DOM. The dev server also stopped re-importing the components that import an edited `.svelte` file: `$.hmr` already swaps the edited component in place, and re-importing the page re-created every component under it. As in any Svelte setup, the edited component itself restarts from its props, and components elsewhere on the page keep their `$state`.
- **Svelte pages that use `getContext` / `setContext`, including every Svelte router page, no longer fail under `absolute start`**
  `absolute start` bundled its own copy of Svelte into the production server, while Svelte pages load Svelte from node_modules. The two copies kept separate component context, so a page calling `getContext` or `setContext` (the Svelte router does) answered every request with a 500 `lifecycle_outside_component`. The production server now keeps Svelte external when the app has Svelte pages, so there is one copy.
- **Vue pages with `client: 'none'` set through a same-file const skip their unused client bundle**
  The build drops the client bundle of a Vue page registered with `client: 'none'`, but it only recognised a string literal. `client: CLIENT_MODE` with `const CLIENT_MODE = 'none'` in the same file still built an unused hydration bundle. The scanner now resolves same-file `const` strings for `client` and for the `asset(manifest, …)` key, including `as const`, `satisfies` and the shorthand `{ client }`. A value it can't know at build time (an import, a `let`, a call) keeps the client bundle, which still works and just isn't trimmed.

## 0.20.0-beta.169 — 2026-11-12

### Fixed

- **A workspace service never shows ready on a port another program holds**
  `absolute workspace dev` warned that another program held a service's port, then started the service anyway and probed the port for readiness. The other program answered, so the service showed "ready" while every request reached someone else's server, and the service itself exited without saying why. A service whose port another program still holds now refuses to start, naming that program: stop it, or give the service another port.

## 0.20.0-beta.168 — 2026-11-12

### Fixed

- **Pages build without the frameworks they don't use installed**
  A project with Svelte pages but no Vue or Angular installed couldn't build any Svelte page, in dev or with `absolute build`: the non-React client pass failed with `Could not resolve: "vue"`, then `@angular/core`, `@angular/platform-browser` and `@angular/compiler`. The Svelte hydration index imports `@absolutejs/absolute/client`, whose island runtime lazily imports a hydrator per framework, and only the React client pass left frameworks the project doesn't have unresolved. The non-React, island and worker client passes, and the dev rebuilds of Svelte and Vue pages, now resolve a framework the project neither configures nor installs to a stub that throws only if that framework's hydrator runs. A bare external wouldn't do: dev island bundles aren't code-split, so Bun hoists the import and the browser can't load the bundle. An installed framework is bundled as before. Verified with a Svelte-only, a Vue-only, and an HTML project with a React island, each in `absolute dev`, `absolute start` and `absolute compile`.
- **Static-page islands hydrate with only `islands.registry`, or a bootstrap file of any name** (`createIslandManifestResolver`)
  Islands on HTML and HTMX pages server-rendered but never hydrated unless the islands bootstrap file happened to compile to the manifest key `BootstrapClient`, the only key the server looked for. A configured `islands.bootstrap` is now recorded under a reserved manifest key whatever its file name. With only `islands: { registry }` set, the build generates a default bootstrap that loads each island's chunk from the manifest, so no bootstrap file is needed. `createIslandManifestResolver()` defaults to the manifest the server injects. React islands now share one React vendor with the bootstrap even without a `reactDirectory`; before, a separately bundled bootstrap brought a second React and hydration failed on `useState`. A page with islands but no bootstrap now logs a warning outside production. Verified in Chromium: `load`, `idle` and `visible` hydrate, `none` doesn't, and React, Svelte and Vue islands hydrate on HTML and HTMX pages.
- **Svelte page props are type-checked in server files**
  `handleSveltePageRequest<typeof Page>({ props })` accepted any props in a server file. Svelte's ambient `*.svelte` module types every import as `LegacyComponentType`, whose props are `Record<string, any>`, and svelte-check only covers the Svelte directory. `absolute typecheck` now generates a declaration per component with svelte2tsx, the engine svelte-check uses, under `.absolutejs/types/svelte/`, and resolves server imports to them through `rootDirs`. A missing prop now fails with TS2741, a wrong type with TS2322 and an unknown prop with TS2353, as for React. `absolute dev` keeps the declarations current as components change. For editor squiggles, add `"rootDirs": [".", ".absolutejs/types/svelte"]` to tsconfig.json (typecheck prints this hint when it's missing). The check needs `svelte2tsx` installed (`bun add -d svelte2tsx`), and typecheck says so when it isn't. Unchanged projects reuse the last declarations. Vue pages were already checked by vue-tsc, and Angular's `requestContext` by its `Ctx` generic.

## 0.20.0-beta.167 — 2026-11-09

### Fixed

- **Refresh imported CSS, stylesheet dependencies, and changed image assets during HMR**
  CSS imported by JavaScript remained in stale style nodes while style-update only reloaded linked bundles. Refresh source stylesheet modules in place to preserve cascade order, rebuild configured CSS entries when imported partials change outside stylesConfig, and run CSS-only incremental builds. Static asset updates now invalidate matching image and favicon URLs. The dev launcher selects patched Bun 1.4.4+absolute.2. React, CSS, logo, and favicon changes were verified in an open Job Tracker page without navigation.

## 0.20.0-beta.166 — 2026-11-06

### Fixed

- **Production client bundles use the production build of every package**
  Production client bundles compiled `process.env.NODE_ENV` as development, because Bun.build does so unless told otherwise, whatever the environment says. React's own vendor build was already fixed, but anything else a page bundled took its development build. That made bundles larger and slower, and could pair a package's development code with production React: the reconciler inside @react-three/fiber reads React's `actQueue`, which production React doesn't have, and threw on absolutejs.ai's billing page. React, other-framework, island and worker client builds now say production in a production build. Development builds are unchanged.

## 0.20.0-beta.165 — 2026-11-05

### Added

- **Expose a server-side tunnel relay entry point with exact callback route restrictions and optional hosting liveness endpoint**

## 0.20.0-beta.164 — 2026-11-02

### Fixed

- **`absolute typecheck` works for projects whose tsconfig sets outDir**
  `absolute typecheck` failed with TS6059 on every source file of a project whose tsconfig sets `outDir`. TypeScript 7 requires every file to sit under rootDir even when nothing is emitted, and with rootDir unset it defaults to the directory of the generated config, `.absolutejs`, whenever outDir is set; the AbsoluteJS docs site reported 20 such errors and its CI had to use plain tsc. bun check never emits, so its generated config now roots the check at the filesystem root, which contains every file it reads, including a script kept beside the project. Real type errors are reported as before; tsc's incremental check keeps the project root.

## 0.20.0-beta.163 — 2026-11-02

### Fixed

- **Stopping `absolute start` also stops the server it started**
  Stopping an `absolute start` that had built (not `--prebuilt`) with SIGTERM left the server it spawned running and holding its port. The build directory lock handles SIGTERM by releasing its locks and exiting, and its handler is registered while the build runs, before `absolute start` installs the one that stops the server, so the process exited first. `absolute start` now also stops its server from an `exit` listener, which runs on any exit, `process.exit` included, as `absolute dev` already does for its child.

## 0.20.0-beta.162 — 2026-11-02

### Fixed

- **Apps share one copy of typebox, exact-mirror, the Elysia plugins and pwa with the framework** (`prepare`)
  The framework pinned packages apps install themselves to exact versions: typebox 1.3.16, exact-mirror 1.2.6, @elysia/static, @elysia/openapi and @elysia/server-timing 2.0.0-rc.0, and @absolutejs/pwa 0.16.3. An app on any other version got a second copy nested under the framework, and for typebox that is a correctness hazard, not bloat: Elysia validates with the app's typebox, and a schema built by a different copy is foreign to it. renown could not move to typebox 1.4 for this reason (2026-11-01). They are now ranges within the same major (pwa within 0.16 and 0.17, whose 0.17.0 only adds asset-failure recovery), and the framework's own tests run on the newest of each: typebox 1.4.3, Elysia 2.0.0-rc.1, pwa 0.17.0.

## 0.20.0-beta.161 — 2026-11-01

### Changed

- **Production servers no longer import absolute.config.ts at runtime** (`prepare`)
  A production server imported absolute.config.ts from source at every boot, through `prepare()` and again in the `absolute start --prebuilt` controller. That evaluated the framework's own unbundled package and everything the config imports beside the server bundle that already contains it: the AbsoluteJS docs site's config imported its sitemap routes, which pulled in every docs page, its data and its highlighter, about 735 modules and roughly 70 MB of the server's memory plus 55 MB of the controller's. `absolute start` and `absolute prepare` now write the plain-data fields the runtime reads to `absolute-runtime.json` in the build directory, and a production `prepare()` (with `ABSOLUTE_BUILD_DIR` set, as `absolute start` sets it) and a prebuilt start read that instead of importing the config. A build without the file, from an older framework or another pipeline, loads the config as before. Production `prepare()` also no longer scans and reads every page source at boot for island metadata that only dev rebuilds use.

## 0.20.0-beta.160 — 2026-10-28

### Fixed

- **Signed iOS builds find their Xcode scheme on a fresh checkout** (`resolveAbsoluteIosXcodeProject`)
  Capacitor 8 ships no shared Xcode scheme and its .gitignore excludes xcuserdata, so a fresh checkout such as a GitHub Actions runner has no .xcscheme file. `mobile build ios` and the simulator certification failed there with "iOS release could not find a shared Xcode scheme"; they only worked on a Mac where opening the project in Xcode had created a user scheme. With no shared scheme, the release now asks Xcode for its schemes (`xcodebuild -list -json`) and uses the only one, or the one named after the project (`App` for Capacitor), beside the scheme for each local Swift package. A shared scheme is still used as before, and an explicit scheme still wins. By Gene Graves.

## 0.20.0-beta.145 — 2026-10-22

### Added

- **`absolute fmt` formats with bun fmt, using your Prettier config**
  `absolute fmt` formats with Bun's built-in `bun fmt` (Bun 1.4.4 or newer). It reads the project's existing Prettier configuration (`.prettierrc*`, overrides, `.prettierignore`, `.editorconfig`) and produces the same output as Prettier 3.9, Svelte included, in milliseconds, so it needs no cache. `absolute fmt --check` exits non-zero when files need formatting. On older Bun it says so and points to `absolute prettier`, which stays for projects whose Prettier plugins `bun fmt` doesn't support.

### Changed

- **absolute dev uses the patched Bun 1.4.4 build**
  `absolute dev` now selects AbsoluteJS's patched Bun 1.4.4 (`1.4.4+absolute.1`, installed and signature-checked by bvm) for React Fast Refresh. Stock Bun 1.4.4 still ignores `reactFastRefresh` on `Bun.Transpiler` (oven-sh/bun#32919), so React edits keep component state only on the patched build. The patched build now reports its full version as `Bun.version`, and the install check accepts it. Projects on the 1.4.2 patched build are offered the update.

### Fixed

- **Projects without a tsconfig.json build on Bun 1.4.3 and newer**
  Builds named `./tsconfig.json` to Bun.build whether or not the project had one. Bun ignored the option until 1.4.3; from 1.4.3 it reads it and fails with `Cannot find tsconfig file`, so on Bun 1.4.3+ a project without a tsconfig.json could not build, compile or start its dev client. The tsconfig is now named only when it exists; otherwise Bun finds the nearest one itself, as it did before.
