## 0.20.0-beta.144 — 2026-10-22

### Breaking

- **Requires Elysia 2.0.0-rc.0, @absolutejs/auth 0.101 and @absolutejs/sync 3** (`prepare`, `startDevPrebuild`)
  Elysia 2.0.0-rc.0 renamed every lifecycle hook to its `on` form (request → onRequest, beforeHandle → onBeforeHandle, afterHandle → onAfterHandle, afterResponse → onAfterResponse, error → onError, parse → onParse, transform → onTransform) and removed setup/cleanup in favour of onStart/onStop. The framework now builds, tests and ships against Elysia 2.0.0-rc.0 and the matching @elysia plugins, and requires `elysia ^2.0.0-rc.0`, so it also accepts later release candidates and 2.0.0. It moves with the packages that made the same change: @absolutejs/auth 0.101 and @absolutejs/sync 3, plus pwa, sync-capacitor and sync-expo releases that accept sync 3.
  _Migration:_ Upgrade `elysia` and every `@elysia/*` package to 2.0.0-rc.0 or later, `@absolutejs/auth` to 0.101 or later and `@absolutejs/sync` to 3. Then rename lifecycle hooks in your server: request → onRequest, beforeHandle → onBeforeHandle, afterHandle → onAfterHandle, afterResponse → onAfterResponse, error → onError, parse → onParse, transform → onTransform; replace setup/cleanup with onStart/onStop. The codemod at absolutejs/scripts codemods/elysia-rc-hooks.ts does the renames (run it before upgrading Elysia).

## 0.20.0-beta.143 — 2026-10-22

### Fixed

- **Browser test recordings and reports no longer restart absolute dev**
  Running a visible Playwright test with screenshots, video or tracing caused absolute dev to repeatedly restart the application: test-results, playwright-report, blob-report and .playwright-mcp were treated as source changes. These generated directories, including their creation and removal, are now ignored by the shared watcher. Atomic-write recovery also honors ignored paths, so temporary trace writes cannot reintroduce generated files into the rebuild queue. Real test source and application assets remain watched.
- **`absolute dev` runs apps that import their own workspace packages, under Bun's isolated or hoisted linker, with hot reload**
  An app that imports one of its own workspace packages (`"@acme/core": "workspace:*"`) did not run under `absolute dev`. With Bun's isolated linker, the default for a workspace, the dev build imported the package from the framework's own folder, could not find it, and the server crash-looped. With the hoisted linker the page rendered but never hydrated: modules outside the app's folder were addressed as `/@src/../…`, which a browser collapses before asking, so they 404ed. Now a package that resolves to source outside node_modules is the app's own code: served and transpiled like the app's files rather than vendored, its folder watched, and an edit to it hot-reloads in place (server and browser) instead of restarting the server or reloading the page. Packages are read from the app's folder, so any dependency only the app declares also works under the isolated linker, and the dev server serves files outside the app folder (a workspace package, a node_modules hoisted to the workspace root) through `/@src/@up/…`. A `dev.watchDirs` entry or a symlink written to work around this is no longer needed.
- **Fresh installs declare the Elysia API version this release supports**
  The broad prerelease peer range allowed Elysia 2.0.0-rc.0 and beta.32, which removed the request lifecycle method used by this framework release. The Elysia peer now requires 2.0.0-beta.21, matching the version used and verified by the framework. Fresh-package acceptance reads that peer contract instead of maintaining a separate stale Elysia range.

## 0.20.0-beta.141 — 2026-10-19

### Added

- **Production serves brotli and gzip copies of static text assets, written at build time**
  Production served every asset uncompressed, so browsers downloaded scripts, stylesheets and HTML files at full size: about three times the bytes, which on a slow network is most of the wait. Production builds now write brotli (quality 9) and gzip copies beside each text asset that compression shrinks by at least a tenth (about a second for the example app), and the production server sends a copy to a browser that accepts it, with `Content-Encoding`, the original `Content-Type`, `Vary: Accept-Encoding` and the asset's cache policy. React's vendor bundle goes from 181 KB to 53 KB. Nothing is compressed on the fly, so streamed responses (server-sent events, streamed pages) are untouched.

### Fixed

- **HEAD requests answer like GET (status and headers, no body) instead of 404**
  Elysia 2 no longer answers HEAD for a GET route, so every AbsoluteJS app answered HEAD with 404 while GET answered 200, pages and static files alike. Uptime monitors, link checkers, crawlers and validators ask with HEAD and read that as down. `networking()` now adds a HEAD fallback that runs the request as GET and returns its status and headers without a body, compiled executables included. A route the app declares with `.head()` still wins.

## 0.20.0-beta.140 — 2026-10-18

### Fixed

- **Dev pages reconnect after a dropped connection without reloading, and keep trying through long outages**
  When the dev-server socket dropped, `absolute dev` pages polled for about 18 seconds and reloaded as soon as the server answered. On weak wifi every network change became a full reload, refetching every stylesheet and script and losing the page's state, and an outage longer than 18 seconds left the page disconnected until a manual reload. The page now reconnects the socket for up to 30 minutes, backing off from half a second to ten, waits for the network instead of retrying while the browser is offline, and retries at once when the network or the tab returns. It reloads only if it missed something: the server restarted, or sent an update while the page was away. The server now includes when it started and when it last sent an update in the manifest it sends each connecting page. The banner says when the browser is offline.
- **Production builds ship React's production build (react-dom 903 KB → 400 KB, no development checks)**
  Production builds bundled React into its vendor files without setting `process.env.NODE_ENV`, so React picked its development build: `react-dom_client.js` was 903 KB, and React ran its development checks in every production page. Production builds now set `process.env.NODE_ENV` to `"production"`: 400 KB, 81 KB gzipped. Only whitespace is minified; renaming identifiers or minifying syntax across the split vendor chunks makes Bun emit an export named `__INVALID__REF__`, which stopped compiled executables from hydrating. `absolute dev` is unchanged; Fast Refresh needs the development build.
- **Edits to class components and `memo`/`forwardRef` wrappers appear in `absolute dev` without a reload**
  React Fast Refresh updates the components it registered. Editing a module that registers none (a class component, or a `memo`/`forwardRef` wrapper the transpiler does not register) re-ran only that module, and its importer kept rendering the old one, so the edit never showed until a reload. The update now also re-imports the module's importers up to the nearest one that registers a component, so the edit appears and the rest of the page keeps its state.

## 0.20.0-beta.139 — 2026-10-16

### Changed

- **Web applications no longer install Expo, React Native or the Expo code-signing tooling; `absolute mobile` installs them for Expo apps** (`generateAbsoluteExpoCodeSigning`)
  Every AbsoluteJS application used to install Expo and React Native, because the framework depended on `@absolutejs/devices-expo` (which needs both as peers) and on `@expo/code-signing-certificates`. A web application never runs either, but it carried them, and with them packages a vulnerability scan flags with no fixed release (node-forge through the signing certificates, braces through Metro). Both are now optional peer dependencies. `absolute mobile` installs `@absolutejs/devices` and `@absolutejs/devices-expo` into an Expo application the first time it needs them, the way it already installs Capacitor, and `absolute mobile update signing generate` installs `@expo/code-signing-certificates` as a development dependency. The framework no longer bundles node-forge into its CLI. Calling `generateAbsoluteExpoCodeSigning` directly now needs `@expo/code-signing-certificates` installed in the application, and says so if it is not.

## 0.20.0-beta.138 — 2026-10-16

### Changed

- **absolute typecheck uses bun check on Bun 1.4.3+, with its own pass cache**
  On Bun 1.4.3 or later, `absolute typecheck` checks TypeScript with `bun check` instead of tsc: it reads the same tsconfig.json and reports the same errors, about 15x faster with a third of the memory on this repository. bun check keeps no .tsbuildinfo, so a passing run is remembered as a fingerprint of every file and tsconfig it read, and an unchanged project is not checked again. Projects with Vue still use vue-tsc. Set ABSOLUTE_TYPECHECK_CHECKER=tsc to keep tsc, and ABSOLUTE_TYPECHECK_THREADS to cap the threads bun check starts. Stylesheet side-effect imports (`import "./app.css"`) are now declared, which TypeScript 7 requires.

### Fixed

- **Dev no longer refetches a deleted stylesheet on every update, and sends Tailwind style updates only when the CSS changed** (`build`, `compileTailwind`, `compileTailwindConfig`)
  In `absolute dev`, a stylesheet whose source was deleted was refetched on every style update, twice, forever: the HMR client reloads every `<link rel="stylesheet">` on each update and kept the dead link in place after its 404. A page left open while an agent rewrote the project sent thousands of requests for one deleted stylesheet. The client now asks once why a reload failed: a 404 or 410 disables that link (it stays in the document for the framework that rendered it) and it is not fetched again until the manifest points it at a different file; any other failure (a rate limit, a dropped connection) backs off from 1 second up to a minute. The dev server also stopped sending a Tailwind style update for every saved file that Tailwind scans; it now sends one only when the generated CSS changed. `compileTailwind` returns whether its output changed.

## 0.20.0-beta.137 — 2026-10-08

### Fixed

- **absolute compile prints the real error when the executable fails to bundle**
  When the last step of `absolute compile` ("Compiling standalone executable") failed, it printed only `AggregateError: Bundle failed`, because Bun throws by default. It now reports failures as data, like the server bundle step, so each error is printed with its file and message.

## 0.20.0-beta.136 — 2026-10-08

### Added

- **iOS release builds check that a push app is signed for production push**
  An app that uses push notifications is built with the `development` push environment so debug builds sign, and App Store export is expected to switch it to `production` through the distribution profile. If it does not, Apple rejects every installed device's push token and no user receives push, with nothing to show for it. `absolute mobile build ios` now reads the entitlements signed into the exported IPA and fails, explaining the fix, unless `aps-environment` is `production`. Apps that do not use push are not inspected.

## 0.20.0-beta.135 — 2026-10-08

### Fixed

- **Tapping a notification that launches an Expo app now opens its deep link**
  Mobile builds now install `@absolutejs/devices` 0.7.1 and Expo builds `@absolutejs/devices-expo` 0.0.12. On Expo, tapping a notification while the app is closed now reaches `pushNotifications.onAction`, so the notification's deep link opens; before, a tap that launched the app was reported before anything listened and was lost. `@absolutejs/devices/testing` gains a push notifications test capability. Run `absolute mobile sync` to update an existing app.

## 0.20.0-beta.134 — 2026-10-08

### Added

- **Mobile release history can live in a blob store, so CI builds keep serving installed apps** (`NormalizedAbsoluteMobileConfig`)
  Builds keep answering the three most recent mobile releases so installed apps keep working, but that history lived only in the build directory, so a fresh checkout such as a CI run started with none and every installed app was asked to update. Set `mobile.compatibility.store` to a project module whose default export is a blob store (for example `awsS3BlobStore` from `@absolutejs/blob/aws-s3`) and `absolute start` and `absolute compile` read the history from it and write each new release back. Releases that only an existing build directory knows are copied into the store on the first build, and `mobile.compatibility.prefix` keeps several apps or environments in one bucket apart. The store does not change the app's runtime fingerprint.
- **Tapping a push notification opens its deepLink inside the app**
  A push sent with `deepLink` carried it to the device as `absoluteDeepLink`, but tapping the notification only opened the app. Tapping it now opens that page inside the app, in Capacitor and Expo apps alike. The link takes the same route as any other deep link, so only the app's configured HTTPS hosts and its URL scheme are opened; anything else is ignored. Action buttons other than the notification body are still left to the app's own `pushNotifications.onAction` listener.

### Fixed

- **PDF assets are served as application/pdf**
  PDF assets were served without a PDF content type in `absolute dev` and in compiled apps, so browsers could download them instead of opening them. They are now served as `application/pdf`.

## 0.20.0-beta.133 — 2026-10-06

### Changed

- **The patched Bun for React Fast Refresh is installed and verified by bvm**
  `absolute dev` and `absolute bun-patch` now install AbsoluteJS's patched Bun with bvm (`@absolutejs/bvm`, a new dependency), which checks the release's checksum list against the AbsoluteJS release key's Ed25519 signature before anything runs. The CLI no longer downloads and unzips the build itself or pins a SHA-256 per platform, so a new patched build no longer needs a framework release. A patched build installed by an earlier release in `~/.absolutejs/bun` moves onto bvm's copy on the next `absolute dev`. bvm has builds for Linux, macOS and Windows on x64 and arm64; FreeBSD and Android no longer get the offer.

## 0.20.0-beta.132 — 2026-10-06

### Fixed

- **Production server bundles inline optional peers that are installed beside their dependency**
  Since 0.20.0-beta.126, `absolute start`, `prepare` and `compile` left a dependency's optional peer external whenever it was missing from the project's own `node_modules`. Under Bun's isolated installs a peer the dependency does have is linked beside that dependency instead, and Bun's `external` list applies to every importer, so installed packages (for example `@neondatabase/serverless` and `zod`) were left as bare imports the production server could not resolve, and it exited at startup with `Cannot find module`. Whether an optional peer is missing is now decided for each import, from the importing file: it is bundled when that file can resolve it, and left external only when it truly is not installed.

## 0.20.0-beta.131 — 2026-10-06

### Added

- **The HTTPS dev server speaks HTTP/2**
  With `dev: { https: true }`, the dev server now also serves HTTP/2 on the same port (Bun 1.4.1+ `http2`), so the browser fetches page modules multiplexed over one connection instead of HTTP/1.1's six per origin, which matters most on import-heavy pages and remote dev hosts. The HMR WebSocket is unchanged: browsers open it as a separate HTTP/1.1 connection on the same port. Plain HTTP dev servers are unaffected.

### Changed

- **AbsoluteJS now requires Bun 1.4.2**
  `engines.bun` is now `>=1.4.2`. Bun 1.4.1 is skipped on purpose: it shipped a `bun build` regression that renamed a nested `var` to a `let` binding's name (`SyntaxError: Cannot declare a var variable that shadows a let/const/class variable`), which 1.4.2 fixes. One behavior change reaches compiled apps: a response whose body stream errors before its first byte is flushed now drops the connection instead of arriving as a complete, empty `200`, so clients see the failure instead of a truncated success.
- **Elysia is now 2.0.0-beta.21**
  AbsoluteJS depends on, and peers with, Elysia `2.0.0-beta.21` (from `2.0.0-beta.6`). Apps should move to the same version. One change can surface in your code: in a general `.error()` handler, `error` is now typed `unknown`, since anything can be thrown, so read its message with `error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)`. Deferred plugins (`lazyPlugin`) now republish the route table through Elysia's public fetch handler, because the internal method they used became private.
- **Exports that return Elysia apps or plugins carry Elysia 2.0.0-beta.21's types** (`prepare`, `startDevPrebuild`, `absoluteRequestContext`, `devtoolsJson`, `createAbsoluteMobileAssociationPlugin`, `createAbsoluteMobileCompatibilityDispatcher`, `createAbsoluteMobilePreviewPlugin`, `createAbsoluteMobileUpdateServerPlugin`)
  These exports return Elysia app and plugin types, so their generated declarations follow Elysia 2.0.0-beta.21: Elysia's own types are now referenced from `elysia` instead of `elysia/types`, and the route map `prepare` returns is inferred by the newer Elysia. Their parameters and runtime behavior are unchanged; code that uses them against the same Elysia version needs no changes.

### Fixed

- **React Fast Refresh is offered again on Bun 1.4.1 and newer**
  Stock Bun still ignores `reactFastRefresh` on `Bun.Transpiler` in 1.4.2 (oven-sh/bun#32919). The patched build `absolute dev` offers was Bun 1.4.0, and the CLI never replaces a newer Bun with an older patched one, so anyone on Bun 1.4.1 or 1.4.2 lost the offer and React edits fell back to a remount. The CLI now offers `bun-v1.4.2-absolute.1`, Bun 1.4.2 with only that fix, checked against its pinned SHA-256 for every platform.

## 0.20.0-beta.130 — 2026-10-03

### Changed

- **Server edits to plugins and the entry are served in hundreds of milliseconds, and slow ones say why**
  Each in-place swap compiled every route of the new Elysia app up front, which took about 2 seconds per edit on an app with a large route table. The new app now builds its router on the first request and compiles each route when that route is first hit, so a plugin or entry edit is served in a few hundred milliseconds. A slow update also names its slowest statements, and an edit to the server entry reports how long it took and which statements re-ran.

### Fixed

- **The dev server starts when a server module re-exports with inline `type` specifiers**
  With 0.20.0-beta.129, a server module re-exporting with an inline `type` specifier (`export { x, type T } from "./x"`) failed to parse in development (`Expected "}" but found "T"`), and the dev server could not start. Re-exports are now loaded with the module's own TypeScript loader.
- **Server edits update in place in the published package instead of restarting**
  In 0.20.0-beta.129 the published package bundles the dev bootstrap separately from the code that reacts to file changes, and each bundle kept its own copy of the hot runtime's state. The file-change side never saw what the bootstrap had installed, so every server edit was reported as not hot-managed and restarted the server, which is the behaviour backend HMR was meant to remove. The state now lives on `globalThis`, so every bundle shares one runtime. A server edit now updates in place in the published package as well, at about 50–250ms for a handler and about 150–300ms for a plugin or the server entry on a large app.
- **Saving a file next to the server entry, or soon after a checkout, no longer restarts or rebuilds unrelated code**
  Two causes of unneeded restarts are fixed. First, the CLI restarted the server for any file saved in the server entry's own folder, including code modules next to the entry. The server process already updates those in place, or asks for a restart when it cannot, so the CLI now leaves code, documents and tests to it and restarts only for other files there (such as `.env`). Second, after a checkout or pull, the first save in a folder made the dev server treat every recently touched file there as edited. A file that has not changed since the dev server started is no longer reported as an edit.

## 0.20.0-beta.129 — 2026-10-03

### Added

- **Server code edits in development update the running server in place instead of restarting it** (`onHotDispose`)
  Editing a server module in development used to restart the whole server: a second or more of downtime, every open page dropped, every connection, pool, queue worker and in-memory cache rebuilt. Server modules are now updated in place, statement by statement. A save re-runs only the top-level statements whose own text changed, those that use something that changed, and the importer statements that call a changed export; everything else (database pools, workers, caches, `let` state) is kept as it was. React pages and components the server imports for SSR are updated the same way, so the next request renders the edit. A handler edit typically lands in 1–50ms with nothing else re-run, and exactly one update is applied per save. What a replaced statement started is stopped before its replacement runs: intervals, timeouts and timer chains (cron libraries included), immediates, `process` listeners, extra `Bun.serve` servers (a fixed port is handed over), workers and `onHotDispose` callbacks. Work started by requests and WebSocket events is never stopped. Rebuilding the Elysia app swaps it onto the running server and runs the old app's `cleanup` and the new app's `setup` hooks, as a stop followed by a listen would. An edit that fails to parse or throws while running keeps the previous version serving, and everything it started is rolled back; the fix applies normally. Set `ABSOLUTE_BACKEND_HMR=0` to restart on server edits as before. See docs/BACKEND_HMR.md.

### Fixed

- **Ember and Angular pages and streaming slots render the rebuilt code after an edit**
  In development the Ember and Angular page handlers re-imported a rebuilt page as a `file:` URL with a `?t=` query, and static streaming slot modules were loaded the same way. Bun ignores the query of a `file:` URL and returned the module it had already loaded, so server-rendered HTML kept the old page. `bun --hot` used to hide this by re-evaluating everything. Each now imports a plain path with the query, which Bun does treat as a new module. The mobile build's capture of the server app had the same problem and is fixed too.
- **A React page no longer goes blank when an edit changes both a component and its CSS**
  When a stylesheet changed, the dev client loaded a copy of its `<link>` and removed the original. React 19 hoists a page's `<link>` elements into `<head>` and still owns them, so the next React remount failed with `Failed to execute 'removeChild' on 'Node'` and the page went blank until reloaded. This happened whenever a component edit also changed Tailwind output. The original `<link>` now stays in the document and takes the new stylesheet once the copy has loaded, so nothing flashes unstyled.
- **Editing a module shared by server and pages rebuilds every page that imports it**
  Since 0.20.0-beta.128, editing a module shared by server and frontend code (a formatter, a constants file) could update the server but leave pages of other frameworks importing it on the old code until the next page edit. Frontend dependents of every framework are now rebuilt when a shared module changes.
- **Saving a file next to an unchanged `absolute.config.ts` no longer restarts the dev server**
  Editors and tools that save by writing a temporary file and renaming it make the dev server rescan the folder for recently touched files. A freshly checked-out or copied `absolute.config.ts` counted as changed even when its contents were the same, and the server restarted. It restarted once from the entry watcher and once more from the rebuild watcher. The config is now handled only by the entry watcher, and only when its contents differ from what the server started with.

### Internal

- **Mobile release artifact declarations list one member in a different order** (`createAbsoluteMobileCompatibilityArtifact`, `parseAbsoluteMobileCompatibilityArtifact`, `readAbsoluteMobileMaterializedReleases`)
  The emitted declarations of these functions list the `generation` member of their inferred object types in a different position. Their types are unchanged.

## 0.20.0-beta.128 — 2026-10-03

### Fixed

- **A page that fails to build in development shows the real build error and reloads itself once fixed** (`DeferredPageAssets`, `DevPageWarmer`)
  When a page failed its on-demand build in development, the handler threw `Asset "<Page>" not found in manifest.` and left the response to whichever error handler answered first. An app with its own `onError` (most real apps) showed its generic error page, so the actual cause — a missing import, a syntax error — was only in the terminal. Page handlers for Vue, React, Svelte, Angular and Ember now return a Build Error page themselves, with the build's own error message, and the page reloads by itself once a rebuild lands or the dev server comes back. AbsoluteJS's fallback error page for missing assets shows the same build error.
- **Editing docs, tests or code the server never loaded no longer restarts the dev server**
  Any changed file no HMR pipeline handled restarted the dev server, including documentation and test files the server never runs. Each restart dropped every open page for seconds and rebuilt them from nothing. Now documents (`.md`, `.txt`, …) and test files never restart it; code modules restart it only when the running server process has loaded them (a module nothing has imported yet loads fresh on first use); config such as `.env`, `package.json` and `tsconfig.json` still does.

## 0.20.0-beta.127 — 2026-10-03

### Fixed

- **Projects on `@absolutejs/auth` 0.97 no longer get a second, older copy**
  AbsoluteJS accepted `@absolutejs/auth` only below 0.97, so a project on auth 0.97 got a second, older copy nested under AbsoluteJS. It now accepts auth up to 0.97. Between 0.96.0 and 0.97.0 the `@absolutejs/auth/client/mobile` declarations are byte-identical, and its runtime differs only in bundler helpers and local variable names.
- **Vue pages whose prop types come through a directory index build again instead of failing with EISDIR**
  Vue resolves an imported prop or emit type by probing the import path as written before trying `<path>.ts` and `<path>/index.ts`. AbsoluteJS answered that probe with `existsSync`, which is true for a directory, so Vue read the directory and the page failed to build with `EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read`. In development the page then answered `Asset "<Page>" not found in manifest`. Any type reached through `export * from './folder'` triggered it, which includes `@absolutejs/auth` 0.97's declarations. Type resolution and CSS `@import` inlining now accept only regular files.

## 0.20.0-beta.126 — 2026-10-01

### Fixed

- **Apps that skip a dependency's optional peer bundle for production again**
  The production server bundle (`absolute prepare`, `absolute start`, `absolute compile`) resolves every import up front, including a dependency's guarded dynamic import of an optional peer. An app using `@absolutejs/auth` without its optional `@node-saml/node-saml` failed with `Could not resolve: "@node-saml/node-saml"` and `Server bundle failed`, so it could never start in production. Optional peers of the app's direct dependencies that are not installed are now left external: the import fails only if that feature is used.

## 0.20.0-beta.125 — 2026-09-29

### Fixed

- **Vue pages that reach a helper through a re-export build again**
  The Vue build copies every `.ts` helper a page reaches into its generated tree, but it found them with a regex that only matched `import … from`. A helper reached only through a re-export (`export { x } from './y'` or `export * from './y'`) was never copied, so the build failed with `Could not resolve: "./y"` and every page above it answered 500 in dev. Dependencies are now read with Bun's import scanner, which sees imports, dynamic imports and all three re-export forms; a regex that also covers re-exports is the fallback for source that does not parse.

## 0.20.0-beta.124 — 2026-09-28

### Fixed

- **Projects on a current `@absolutejs/auth` no longer get a second, older copy**
  AbsoluteJS accepted `@absolutejs/auth` only below 0.77, so a project that added a current auth (0.77 to 0.96) got two copies: its own, plus 0.76.3 nested under AbsoluteJS for the mobile shell. The duplicate also doubled the auth type declarations TypeScript loads. AbsoluteJS now accepts auth up to 0.96. The `@absolutejs/auth/client/mobile` API it uses is byte-identical from 0.76.3 to 0.96.0, in both its declarations and its runtime.
- **`/hmr-status` no longer counts closed or duplicate HMR clients** (`HMRWebSocket`)
  Elysia 2 hands every open, message and close event of a WebSocket a new wrapper object. The dev server tracked HMR clients by that wrapper, so a closed browser tab was never removed (it stayed until a broadcast send threw) and each `ready` message counted the same tab again under `connectedTargets`, so `/hmr-status` reported clients that were gone and more web targets than open sockets. Clients are now tracked by the underlying socket.

## 0.20.0-beta.123 — 2026-09-28

### Added

- **React Fast Refresh keeps component state: `absolute dev` can run on AbsoluteJS's patched Bun**
  Stock Bun ignores `reactFastRefresh` on `Bun.Transpiler` (oven-sh/bun#32919), so React edits in `absolute dev` remounted the page and lost component state. AbsoluteJS now publishes Bun 1.4.0 with just that fix for every platform Bun ships (github.com/absolutejs/patched-bun). In React projects on stock Bun, `absolute dev` offers it once (Install now / Ask me later / Don't ask again); it installs to ~/.absolutejs/bun, is checked against a pinned SHA-256, and only the dev server uses it, so your `bun` is unchanged. `absolute bun-patch [status|install|remove|reset]` manages it; `ABSOLUTE_PATCHED_BUN=0` opts out.

### Fixed

- **`absolute dev` keeps rebuilding after a syntax error in a React component or an unhandled rejection**
  Under `bun --hot`, Bun counts unhandled rejections that no listener claims and never resets the count; while it is non-zero Bun parks the process in a loop that still serves requests and delivers file-watch events but never runs timers. The server entry imports React pages, so saving a React component with a syntax error made Bun's hot reload reject, and from then on the HMR debounce never fired: every edit was detected and queued, including the one that fixed the error, and nothing rebuilt until the dev server restarted. An unhandled rejection in app code did the same. The dev server now claims unhandled rejections and prints them as before, so its timers keep running.
- **The patched Bun is now a release build, not a canary build**
  `absolute bun-patch install` and the `absolute dev` offer now install `bun-v1.4.0-absolute.2`. The first release was built as a Bun canary build (Bun's build default): it reported `1.4.0-canary.1`, enabled Bun's experimental "bake" server features and made `bun upgrade` track canary. absolute.2 is built with `--canary=off`, as Bun's own releases are; the React Fast Refresh fix is unchanged. Run `absolute bun-patch install` to replace an absolute.1 install.
- **Removed a React HMR CSS branch that only matched the example app**
  The React HMR client had a CSS-only branch that looked up the example app's `ReactExampleCSS` manifest key, so it could never work in another app; the server never sends a CSS-only React update, so it was also unreachable. Removed. Stylesheet edits on React pages go through the general stylesheet swap, now covered by a browser test (the rule applies, component state and the document are kept).
- **React edits that add a component, touch a hook or utility, or create a folder now update the page in place**
  The React fast path told the browser to re-import a single module: the first non-page file in the batch. A new component added to the page re-imported only the new file, so the page never rendered it; a folder created alongside a file became the target and its URL failed to load; and an edited hook or utility whose importer had not been fetched through the module server re-imported just itself, which updates nothing on screen. Every edited file now gets a target (hooks and utilities resolve to the nearest importing component, falling back to the dependents the dependency graph found), directories and deleted paths are skipped, and the client imports them all before refreshing. On stock Bun the remount fallback rendered the changed child in place of the whole page; it now re-imports the page module for the page on screen and ignores edits that do not reach it.
- **React Fast Refresh is used when Bun supports it, instead of always falling back to a remount**
  The dev server decides between React Fast Refresh and the stock-Bun remount fallback by transpiling a probe component. The probe was named `__AbsoluteRefreshProbe`; React Fast Refresh registers only capitalized components, so it reported "unsupported" even on a Bun with the reactFastRefresh fix, and React edits always remounted with a warning. It now uses a capitalized name.
- **A syntax error in a React component shows the error overlay instead of reloading the page**
  A React edit that failed to compile was still broadcast as an update. The browser imported a module that answered 500 and fell back to a full reload, which showed the last good page and no error. The dev server now checks the edited modules compile first and sends the error overlay (file, line and source line) instead; the save that fixes it applies as a normal in-place update. The module server handler and its transform errors also moved to globalThis: after a `bun --hot` reload failed part-way, later imports of the module server got a fresh instance that was never configured, so pre-transforming the changed module silently did nothing.

- **Preserve browser-translated attributes and inserted text-only font wrappers through hydration** (`captureSsrTextBaselines`, `prepareBrowserTranslationHydration`, `preserveBrowserTranslation`)
  Snapshot alt, title, placeholder and aria-label alongside SSR text. Temporarily restore those attributes and newly inserted text-only font trees while the framework hydrates, then reapply translations on the hydrated nodes. Preserve authored and interactive markup, URLs, field values and genuine client changes. Fixes translated landing-page warnings and text reverting to English without suppressing ordinary hydration mismatches.

## 0.20.0-beta.121 — 2026-09-27

### Added

- **`absolute db backup` and `restore` work on every SQL engine Drizzle and Prisma support, not only PostgreSQL**
  The engine is picked from the URL scheme (with drizzle.config dialect / Prisma provider as a fallback): PostgreSQL and CockroachDB, MySQL, MariaDB and SingleStore, SQLite and local libSQL files, remote libSQL/Turso (optional peer @libsql/client) and SQL Server (optional peer mssql). Dependency order, identifier quoting, upserts and value encoding are per dialect; generated columns are skipped and identity columns are inserted explicitly. MongoDB and Gel are refused with a clear message. `absolute db seed --url` hands the URL and engine to the seed script. PostgreSQL backups keep their exact file shape.

### Fixed

- **`absolute db restore` into PostgreSQL keeps JSON documents, arrays, bytea, identity columns and sequences intact**
  json/jsonb values were stringified before binding, and Bun SQL JSON-encodes bound values, so every document was restored as a JSON string scalar. Array columns failed to bind, bytea values are now decoded from their backed-up Buffer JSON, `generated always` identity and generated columns were rejected, and serial/identity sequences were left behind the restored ids so the next insert collided.
- **Starting a server no longer kills unrelated processes that hold its port**
  `absolute start`, `compile`, the config server and `workspace` cleared their port by killing every process listening on it, including unrelated services and other projects' servers (a PostgreSQL, another app, a control plane). They now stop only a leftover AbsoluteJS server started from this project directory, and report anything else on the port as left running.
